name: Villa Dubrovnik
positioning: Cliffside hotel above the Adriatic facing Lokrum Island and Dubrovnik's Old Town, renovated by Studio Arthur Casas
best_for: Travelers who want sea views of the Old Town and Lokrum from a cliffside base
Families wanting suites with interconnecting rooms

facts.text: Villa Dubrovnik is perched on a cliff, with views of the island of Lokrum and the Old Town.
The building was designed in 1961 by architect Mladen Frka as a residence for members of political elites in Dubrovnik's Sveti Jakov area.
In 1963 the building became an annex to Hotel Argentina.
Room interiors were designed by Studio Arthur Casas.
The hotel displays works by local Croatian painters and sculptors such as Ivana Pegan, Dubravka Tullio and Ivo Dimnic.
Restaurant Pjerin serves breakfast, lunch and dinner on a glass terrace overlooking the Old Town.
Giardino Restaurant sits under century-old pines on an ancient stone terrace.
Galanto Bar is the hotel's rooftop bar.
Villa Spa treatments combine innovative techniques with Mediterranean natural remedies.
The hotel has an indoor pool with floor-to-ceiling windows facing the sea.
Family suites have interconnecting rooms and balcony hot tubs.
During the winter of 2024 the hotel underwent a complete renovation by Brazilian studio Studio Arthur Casas.

highlights.text: The Villa Kolin Residence sits in a secluded part of the hotel, with private access through a small pine forest and a private pool.
Traditional Croatian lace patterns appear in the rooms as wardrobe decoration.
The suites are named after old Dubrovnik expressions.
The hotel's rocky cliffside beach has jumping platforms into the sea.

considerations.text: The Old Town is a 15-minute walk away, or a private transfer that is part of the hotel's service.
The beach is naturally rocky and not wheelchair accessible.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing reflecting the luxury positioning.
